research_question: What historical model best explains the relationship among Proto-Tarahumara *-ame, seventeenth-century gamek, Steffel -ameke/-ame, and modern -ame/-ami and color -ka/-na morphology?
central_assessment: The continuity of a derivational/participial domain centered on *-ame is now supported at Proto-Tarahumara, seventeenth-century, eighteenth-century and modern levels. This is substantially stronger than a lexical similarity hypothesis. The color subsystem most plausibly reflects retention of older stative/participial material followed by semantic and analogical specialization, but color-specific historical -c/-k = modern -ka remains unproven.

historical_backbone.evidence: Merrill & Burgess 2014 reconstruct *-ame as adjectivalizer/nominalizer and participial material; late PT *-rúame is *-rú- 'be' + participial *-ame.
Guadalaxara's Pedro norugamek, cited and analyzed by Merrill & Burgess 2014, attests a stative gamek chain before Steffel.
Numerous forms in -ameke and attested truncations in -ame; Steffel reports frequent omission of final -ke in pronunciation. Color pairs include čókameke~čókame and rosákameke~rosákame.
Participial -ame is independently described; -ami can be a surface reflex in some varieties. Merrill & Burgess report modern -game = stative -ga- + participial -ame in some dialects.

color_subsystem.bridge_1_participial: Historical čókameke~čókame and rosákameke~rosákame align directly with modern chó-ka-me and rosá-ka-me at the surface level.
color_subsystem.bridge_2_na: Historical tsestá-na 'is red' is explicitly segmented and compared by Merrill with modern sitá-na 'be/become red'; modern multivariety descriptions use -na systematically in color predicates.
color_subsystem.modern_semantic_organization: Modern color paradigms contrast -kame for a stronger/core color reading with -name/-na for lower/intermediate/becoming color readings across multiple varieties.
color_subsystem.historical_segmentation_limit: Published historical analyses do not independently segment the c/k before -(a)meke in Steffel's color forms as a color morpheme -ka.

hypothesis_ranking.summary: Inherited stative/participial ga+ame(+ke) material survived, while color morphology regularized/specialized a pre-participial -ka and contrasted it with -na.
Historical color -cameke/-gameke directly continues older stative/participial morphology, but the modern semantic opposition developed without a reconstructible intermediate stage yet.
An inherited opaque -kame(ke) chain was later resegmented as -ka + -me; possible, but less economical after the Proto-*ame and 1683 gamek evidence.

priority_candidates.interpretation: Grade A remains an evidence-architecture label, not a declaration of demonstrated cognation.

claims_now_supported: A Proto-Tarahumara *-ame can be independently reconstructed.
Stative combinations involving -ame predate Steffel and include a gamek chain in 1683.
Steffel preserves widespread -ameke/-ame alternation including direct color pairs.
Modern Ralámuli independently preserves participial -ame and dialectal stative -ga+-ame.
The color domain contains at least two independent historical-modern morphological bridges: kameke~kame to ka-me, and -na to -na.
claims_still_not_supported: Automatic segmentation of every historical -cameke/-gameke as -ga/-ka + -ame + -ke.
Proof that the c/k of each Steffel color word is identical to modern color -ka.
A securely dated moment when modern color -ka versus -na semantics became specialized.
documentary_limit: Steffel's 1799 Latin grammar remains unpublished according to Estrada Fernández 2021, preventing a full direct search of its adjective/stative morphology in the accessible published corpus.
next_phase: Seek direct access to Steffel 1799 or a scholarly transcription to test ca/ka/ga morphology.
Audit Burgess 1984 and Burgess-Kempton-MacLaury 1983 directly where full text becomes accessible.
Build a controlled k~g correspondence series in relevant morphological environments.
Date the semantic specialization of color -ka versus -na using twentieth-century grammars and elicitation studies.
Keep SRC-02 provenance resolution active as a separate documentary problem.
